text:
Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine poses a serious threat to UK prosperity and security. We are proud to be a leading partner in providing vital support to Ukraine.

In total, the UK has committed over £35.5 billion for Ukraine:

£16.5 billion in military support (including our £2.26 billion Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration (ERA) Loan contribution)

up to £12.6 billion in non-military support (including bilateral assistance and fiscal guarantees)

£6.5 billion cover limit in export finance (via UK Export Finance for reconstruction and defence projects)

Diplomacy

the UK, alongside France, is jointly leading Coalition of the Willing nations’ efforts to support Ukraine’s future security

the UK, France, and Ukraine signed a Declaration of Intent relating to the deployment of multinational forces to Ukraine in the event of a ceasefire (6 January 2026)

the UK-Ukraine 100 Year Partnership is fostering broader and closer collaboration across 9 key pillars, including defence and security, science and technology, and economy and trade (signed at leader-level on 16 January 2025)

British Embassy Kyiv hosted a policy forum to mark the first-year anniversary of the 100 Year Partnership and demonstrate our ambition across political, defence, innovation and recovery pillars (16 January 2026)

the Foreign Secretary met Foreign Minister Sybiha in Kyiv to launch the next iteration of the UK-Ukraine Strategic Dialogue (8 October 2026). The former Prime Minister hosted President Zelenskyy in London to conclude the first year of the Strategic Dialogue, recognising progress across all 8 pillars and identify strategic priorities for the year ahead (17 March 2026)

the UK has supported United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) resolutions condemning:

Russia’s forcible deportation of Ukrainian children: 3 December 2025

Russia’s invasion of Ukraine: 24 February 2026, 24 February 2025, 23 February 2023 and 2 March 2022

Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s critical energy infrastructure, including nuclear facilities: 24 July 2024

Russia’s attempted illegal annexation of 4 eastern Ukrainian regions: 12 October 2022

we regularly use the UN Security Council to condemn Russia’s attacks on Ukraine and reaffirm that Russian disinformation, false accusations and violations of UNSC resolutions and the UN Charter, in addition to wider attempts to undermine the multilateral system, will not deter our steadfast support for Ukraine

we use the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) as a forum to hold Russia accountable:

Minister Doughty reaffirmed the UK’s continued support for Ukraine at a Reinforced Permanent Council on 24 February 2026 to mark 4 years since Russia’s full-scale invasion

UK representatives sit across the table from the Russian delegation to deliver interventions every week, calling out malign Russian behaviour, combatting disinformation and isolating it diplomatically

we have supported the OSCE’s Support Programme for Ukraine financially and highlighted the militarisation and indoctrination of Ukrainian children via the OSCE’s formal fact-finding missions (known as the Moscow Mechanism), having published 6 reports since February 2022

we support the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to strengthen nuclear safety and security in Ukraine, particularly at Ukraine’s ZNPP (Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant). We hold Russia directly accountable for the nuclear safety and security challenges Ukraine now faces, including those resulting from Russia’s missile strikes on Ukraine’s energy grid. We have supported 7 Board of Governors resolutions and 4 General Conference resolutions since 2022 and provided €5 million to the IAEA’s Nuclear Security Fund for Ukraine (7 October 2026)

Military

to date, the UK has committed £16.5 billion in military support for Ukraine since the invasion, which includes our contribution of £2.26 billion to the G7 ‘Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration’ Loan for Ukraine, to be repaid using profits generated by seized Russian assets. We will sustain £3 billion a year in military aid until 2030 to 2031 and for as long as it takes (announced on 10 July 2024)

last year, the UK spent an unprecedented £4.5 billion in support of Ukraine (16 January 2025). This year the UK has committed an additional £3.5 billion of military support and combined with the third and final instalment of the Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration Loan, will spend a total of £4.25 billion on military support for Ukraine

we have committed over £600 million in air defence support, including a £100 million contribution to NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List to support Ukraine with Patriot missiles and other air defence equipment that will be delivered before the winter (8 September 2026)

we have committed £500 million in military support to help defend Ukraine from attacks this winter (28 October 2026)

the UK agreed that defence firm Matra BAe Dynamics Alenia (MBDA) could release classified information on UK components for the long-range missile, SCALP (24 August 2026)

we will deliver 150,000 drones and 350 air defence missiles by the end of the year (18 June 2026)

the former Prime Minister joined over 24 other Coalition of the Willing leaders in Paris and announced the UK’s participation in the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan initiative giving UK defence firms access to contracts (13 July 2026)

our UK-Ukraine Defence Industrial Support Treaty expanded the range of military equipment that could be funded by drawing on £3.5 billion of export finance (signed on 19 July 2024)

a new UK-Ukraine agreement to share battlefield technology will boost UK drone production for Ukraine (23 June 2025)

we have trained over 67,000 Ukrainian personnel in the UK under Operation INTERFLEX

we administer the International Fund for Ukraine to procure military equipment: over £3 billion has been pledged to the International Fund for Ukraine to date

Non-military

the UK’s non-military commitments to Ukraine since the start of the invasion come to over £12.6 billion. This includes:

up to £9.5 billion in fiscal support through World Bank loan guarantees and a £0.5 billion grant to the World Bank International Development Association’s crisis facility to mobilise £1.5 billion of support to bolster Ukraine’s economic stability and support vital public services. This includes a multi-year commitment announced at the Ukraine Recovery Conference in 2023

up to £1.5 billion committed in bilateral assistance, including a nearly £290 million bilateral assistance package for 2026 to 2027, announced at the Ukraine Recovery Conference 2026 to fund energy security and recovery programmes

Humanitarian

the UK is one of Ukraine’s leading bilateral donors and has committed up to £611 million in humanitarian assistance for Ukraine and the region since the start of the full-scale invasion (8 October 2026). Recent announcements include:

£34 million to protect and maintain heating and water for Ukrainian families ahead of the winter (8 October 2026)

a commitment of £5.7 million to provide humanitarian aid to frontline communities (24 February 2026)

we have committed £100 million in humanitarian assistance in 2025 to 2026, from which £10 million has been allocated to the Ukraine Humanitarian Fund and £8 million for targeted winter assistance (3 December 2025 and 12 November 2025)

since the full-scale invasion, under the Global Mine Action Programme, the UK has provided £15.15 million to HALO Trust for mine action, including a £2.25 million contract extension this year, to support their work in Ukraine, with Mines Advisory Group and Ukrainian Deminers Association as downstream partners. Our demining efforts have released over 1,318,445 square metres of land and provided Explosive Ordnance Risk Education to 137,549 beneficiaries (June 2022 to end September 2026)

Recovery and reconstruction

our contributions to the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), part of the World Bank group, and to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), continue to expand critical war risk insurance cover, boosting trade and investment into Ukraine

our £6.5 billion cover limit in export finance via UK Export Finance has supported critical reconstruction and defence projects in Ukraine. This support has already enabled the reconstruction of 6 key bridges in the Kyiv region and the delivery of mine countermeasure vessels

through our development finance institution, British International Investment (BII), we are working in partnership with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to make trade finance available to support critical imports and exports to and from Ukraine. BII will deliver up to £65 million for renewable energy and the banking sector in Ukraine (25 June 2026)

£17 million in funding towards repairs to the Chornobyl nuclear power plant damaged by Russian drone strike last year (15 October 2026)

up to £12 million for a new Governance Programme, which will support efforts on rule of law, justice and anti-corruption (25 June 2026)

a £25 million social recovery programme will support Ukraine to build more inclusive and efficient social protection systems and revitalise community and family-based services (7 February 2025)

a £50 million economic recovery programme will unlock hundreds of millions of pounds worth of private lending to bolster the growth and resilience of small and medium businesses in Ukraine (£40 million announced 12 January 2025, £10 million boost announced 5 February 2025)

Energy

overall, the UK has committed over £770 million for energy security and resilience in Ukraine through grant, in-kind support and loan guarantees

as part of this, we have committed £193 million to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund to support repairs, protection and power generation

this includes £107 million in energy support announced since September 2025 to support repairs and replacement of power generation infrastructure and put in place critical protection (8 October 2026, 24 February 2026, 16 January 2026, 12 November 2025 and 12 September 2025)

a further £1 million in support of Ukraine’s Green Transition Office was confirmed at the Ukraine Recovery Conference in July 2025, and a further £700,000 was announced at URC26 (25 June 2026)

we have committed £17 million for a second round of the UK’s Innovate Ukraine Green Energy Competition, bringing our total investment to £34 million. This will support UK and Ukrainian innovators to help rebuild a greener and more resilient energy grid (9 December 2025)

we have provided UK Export Finance loan guarantees to secure nuclear fuel for Ukraine, including a £181 million guarantee in 2024 and a further £210 million deal announced in June 2026 for Urenco to supply nuclear fuel to Energoatom for the next 2 years (15 June 2026)

Sanctions

the UK has sanctioned over 3,500 individuals, entities and ships under the Russia sanctions regime, over 3,300 of which have been sanctioned since Putin’s full-scale invasion

the UK is able to interdict Shadow Fleet vessels, allowing the British military to board sanctioned ships transiting UK waters (25 March 2026). The UK, for the first time, successfully intercepted a Russian Shadow Fleet vessel in the English Channel (14 June 2026)

as of October 2026, the UK has specified over 650 vessels under the Russia sanctions regime, including over 600 oil tankers

UK, US and EU sanctions have denied Russia access to almost $500 billion since February 2022.

between October 2024 and September 2025, UK imports from and exports to Russia of all goods dropped by 98.1% and 97.5% compared to 2021

this government has imposed sanctions against:

38 individuals and entities including Russian oil companies, shadow fleet tankers, and those supplying goods critical to Russia’s military (8 October 2026)

31 individuals and entities including LNG shadow fleet vessels, Kremlin disinformation networks and perpetrators of civilian torture and child indoctrination (1 October 2026)

19 individuals and entities enabling Russia’s war in Ukraine, further constraining the networks and revenue streams on which the Kremlin relies (6 August 2026)

24 individuals and entities behind destructive cyber and hybrid operations (13 July 2026). This is the first joint sanctions package with the EU

nearly 300 targets, including critical energy revenues and military equipment suppliers. This is the largest Russia sanctions package since the early months of 2022 (24 February 2026)

War crimes and justice

the UK has provided £22.8 million to support Ukraine’s domestic war crimes investigations

with our EU and US partners, we established the Atrocity Crimes Advisory Group to coordinate our collective technical assistance and capacity building support for Ukraine’s efforts to document, investigate and prosecute atrocity crimes

we have committed more than £4 million to support Ukrainian efforts to facilitate the return and reintegration of children forcibly deported by Russia, including a pilot tracing mechanism which has identified over 20,000 additional children since the beginning of September

we supported the resolution establishing the Operating Model of the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression which was adopted on 15 May, paving the way to hold those responsible for Russia’s war to account

we are a founding member of the Register of Damage for Ukraine, which allows Ukrainians to record losses, injury or damage as a result of the war and open for all 43 claims categories (30 September 2026)

we signed the Council of Europe Convention on the Establishment of an International Claims Commission for Ukraine (16 December 2025)

Trade

the UK-Ukraine Digital Trade Agreement has entered into force, facilitating duty-free digital content trade (1 September 2024)

the UK-Ukraine TechBridge delivers projects in mutual trade, investment, innovation research and digital skills development

the UK’s first dedicated business centre for industry in Ukraine has now opened, offering UK companies a permanent presence in Kyiv to deepen industrial ties with Ukraine (8 October 2026)

our City-Ukraine Hub leverages UK expertise to deliver capacity building projects

our provision of military equipment to deter attacks and insurance through the UK-developed Unity facility has supported the Black Sea maritime corridor and enabled Ukraine to keep exporting its goods. Ukraine exported all of its 2023 and 2024 harvests – crucial for global food security and Ukraine’s economy

the Ukraine Reconstruction Project Development Programme is a pilot programme set up by DBT to fund feasibility and scoping studies by British businesses for major reconstruction projects (1 July 2026)

UK-Ukraine Political, Free Trade and Strategic Partnership Agreement enables UK businesses to benefit from tariff free trade on all goods until 31 March 2029 (tariffs on eggs and poultry extended until 31 March 2028) (19 January 2026)

For further information visit the Department for Business and Trade’s Ukraine page.

Ukrainians in the UK

237,200 Ukrainians have arrived in the UK, including 177,600 through Homes for Ukraine (as of 31 March 2026)

the Ukraine Permission Extension (UPE) scheme opened on 4 February 2025 providing an additional 18 months permission and a continuation of the same rights and entitlements for Ukrainians in the UK on the Ukraine schemes. 147,186 UPE applications have been granted (as of 31 March 2026)

the Government recently extended the UPE scheme by an additional 24 months. This means individuals coming to the end of their initial 18 months’ permission under UPE can apply for a further 24 months under the scheme, totalling 3.5 years under UPE

the application window for UPE applications has also increased from 28-days to 90-days before an applicant’s current permission expires

English language and employment support is being provided by the UK government-funded STEP programme, a free, 12 or 24 weeks virtual programme open to all Ukrainians living in the UK on one of the humanitarian UK visa schemes

Culture

the UK has contributed over £2.5 million for the protection of Ukrainian cultural heritage across various projects. These include 2 donations to the Ukrainian Cultural Heritage Fund (UCHF), as well as donations of emergency conservation materials to Ukrainian museums

New Ukrainian GCSE to help young Ukrainians preserve their heritage while opening pathways to future education and employment for all pupils [4 Nov 2026]

the Government has supplied funding for the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE)-led Heritage Crime Task Force in Ukraine

the Government has funded Historic England for a programme to provide cultural heritage professionals with support as they work to ensure heritage is protected, preserved, and restored

the Department for Culture, Media, and Sport (DCMS) and the Ministry of Culture for the Government of Ukraine together initiated a Cultural Commission in March 2026. This project provides a forum for collaboration, information exchange, and cultural celebration, and is one of the deliverables under the UK-Ukraine 100-Year Partnership. The British Council and Ukrainian Institute are core members
